title: Intelligent fallback chaining for pinned model versions across regions and variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a multi-stage, policy-driven fallback chain for requests pinned to specific model versions. The goal is to keep pinned workloads online with predictable behavior when a pinned version is unavailable (deprecation, capacity exhaustion, or rollout rollback), without violating customer pinning guarantees more than necessary. This ticket covers the policy model, runtime routing changes, telemetry, migration steps, and deprecation UX hooks.

Background: Currently pinned requests either fail fast or fall back to a single hardcoded variant in the same region. This creates outage risk when that variant is temporarily unavailable or when we deprecate a pinned version. We need a deterministic, auditable fallback chain that considers region preferences, compatible model variants (quantization, sequence length, architecture parity), and deprecation windows.

Goals/Acceptance criteria: 
- Define a fallback policy language (JSON schema) that encodes ordered fallback tiers: (1) exact-version same-region, (2) exact-version cross-region within allowed regions, (3) compatible-variant same-region, (4) compatible-variant cross-region, (5) last-resort "recommended replacement" version.
- Implement runtime routing that evaluates the chain with capacity- and latency-aware guards (only choose an upstream if estimated latency <= configured threshold and capacity flag is healthy).
- Honor customer pinning: only bypass a pin when deprecation TTL or emergency override applies; log an auditable event whenever a pin is bypassed.
- Publish a performance-profile-aware ranking that orders compatible variants by expected tail latency and quality delta (from model onboarding profiles).
- Add metrics and traces for each fallback decision including reason (capacity, deprecation, incompatible settings), chosen candidate, and latency delta.
- Provide a minimal Console UI hook (read-only for first phase) that shows the active fallback chain for a pinned version and recent bypass events.

Design notes: 
- Policy schema: a small, versioned JSON structure attached to model metadata. Example keys: allowed_regions, fallback_tiers (list), deprecation_window_days, emergency_override_expiry. Policies default to conservative behavior: prefer same-region exact-version or fail. Admins/PMs can enable cross-region fallback for global customers.
- Compatibility matching: use model metadata tags (quantization: q4_0/q8_0, max_seq, architecture_id) and onboarding performance profile (token/sec, p95) to compute a compatibility score. Only candidates above a threshold are eligible.
- Capacity/latency guard: the router queries runtime shard health (available_slots, recent_p95) and a per-candidate cost estimate to ensure fallback won't blow budget or violate latency SLO. If guard fails, continue down chain.
- Deprecation handling: when a pinned version is in scheduled deprecation, the runtime should attempt to route to the "recommended replacement" after deprecation_window_days have passed, but only if customer hasn't requested strict no-fallback. All attempts are recorded and customers receive a deprecation notice via console and audit log. Emergency deprecations (security/fix) may force immediate bypass with notification.

Trade-offs and decisions: 
- Simpler option (fail-fast) would preserve pin semantics but yield worse availability. We choose a middle ground: preserve pin intent while offering controlled bypasses and strong observability to protect customers.
- Cross-region fallbacks improve availability but can increase latency and egress costs. This is gated by per-customer policy and a latency guard.
- Quality regression risk is mitigated by using onboarding profiles to avoid candidates with known large deltas; we will provide an opt-out flag for customers wanting absolute fidelity.

Implementation plan: 
1) Policy schema and metadata endpoints (2 wks) — add to model catalog and onboarding pipeline.
2) Match & rank service (2 wks) — offline component that computes compatible candidates and ranking using performance profiles.
3) Router changes (3 wks) — implement chain evaluation, capacity guard, and auditable bypass events. Add unit/integration tests.
4) Telemetry & Console hook (1 wk) — expose fallback traces and an initial read-only chain view.
5) Staged rollout (2 wks) — feature flag per-customer, start with internal accounts then opt-in customers.

Testing plan: 
- Simulation tests using production traffic templates to validate fallback chain behavior and no silent regressions in latency or cost.
- Chaos tests (kill variant nodes, saturate capacity, force deprecations) to verify correct bypass events and fallbacks.
- QA end-to-end with two enterprise customers in staging.

Monitoring / SLOs: 
- New metrics: fallback_attempts_total{reason}, fallback_success_total, fallback_latency_delta_ms_histogram, pin_bypassed_events_total.
- Alerts: spike in fallback_success_total or pin_bypassed_events_total > 0.5% of requests for a customer triggers on-call review.

Rollout and migration: 
- Default policy conservative: no cross-region fallback and require explicit opt-in for non-identical variants.
- Provide a migration guide in Console and PRD linking to model onboarding to add fallback policy when publishing performance profiles.
- Phase 1 read-only Console view, phase 2 allow editing policies via console/SDK.

Follow-ups: 
- Phase 2: enable automated suggestions for replacements based on evals and quality deltas.
- Phase 3: integrate cost-aware routing that factors per-token cost into ranking.
